what_its_for: Butoconazole nitrate is an antifungal cream used to treat vaginal yeast infections (also called vaginal candidiasis). It works by killing the fungus (Candida) that causes the infection, helping to relieve itching, burning, and abnormal discharge.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as a vaginal cream and is inserted directly into the vagina using the applicator provided. Wash your hands before and after use. Lie on your back with your knees bent. Gently insert the filled applicator as far into the vagina as is comfortable, then slowly push the plunger to release the cream. Remove the applicator. You may want to wear a panty liner to protect your underwear from any leakage. Use this medicine at bedtime to help it stay in place while you sleep.
dosing: The usual dose is one full applicator (about 5 grams) of cream inserted into the vagina. Gynazole-1 is a single-dose treatment, meaning you only use it one time. Femstat 3 is used once a day at bedtime for 3 days in a row. Always follow the directions on your prescription label or as told by your doctor.
missed_dose: If you are using the 3-day treatment and miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not use two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you used the single-dose treatment (Gynazole-1), there is only one dose, so a missed dose does not apply.
storage: Store butoconazole nitrate cream at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the tube tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze the cream. Keep it away from heat and direct light. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the cream after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid sexual intercourse while using this medicine, or make sure your partner uses a condom, as the cream may weaken latex condoms and diaphragms, making them less effective. Do not use tampons, douches, or other vaginal products while being treated unless your doctor tells you it is okay. Avoid getting the cream in your eyes. Do not use this medicine if you are allergic to butoconazole or any of its ingredients.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if: your symptoms do not improve within 3 days or do not go away completely within 7 days of treatment; your symptoms come back within 2 months; you develop severe burning, itching, or irritation in or around the vagina after using this cream; you have stomach pain, fever, or chills; you have a bad-smelling vaginal discharge; you are pregnant or think you might be pregnant; or you are not sure if you have a yeast infection, as other infections can look similar and may need different treatment.
when_it_works: Most women start to feel some relief from symptoms like itching and burning within 1 to 3 days of starting treatment. However, it is important to finish the full course of treatment even if you feel better sooner. If you used the single-dose treatment, you may still experience some relief within 1 to 3 days, but full improvement may take up to a week.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant. It is generally not recommended during the first 3 months of pregnancy. During the second and third trimesters, it should only be used if your doctor says it is necessary. Do not use the applicator during pregnancy; instead, use your finger to insert the cream gently. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before using it while breastfeeding. Children: This medicine is only for use in adults. Do not use it in girls who have not yet started their menstrual periods. Older adults: No special dose adjustments are needed for older adults, but always follow your doctor's instructions.
